title: Ship Paper-to-Prod + Phase 5 gate + DSA gate
objective: Deploy the demo, publish the eval report, README, video; take the Phase 5 assessment; log the DSA gate attempt (4/5 unseen mediums ≤35 min). FAANG-tier applications on.
topics: Shipping discipline: README → architecture → eval → limitations
theory: Google project rule; Blueprint Sheet 03 application priority (referral → direct → parallel).
deliverables: Paper-to-Prod v1.0 deployed behind a spend cap; docs/eval-report.md public; demo video
Applications: ≥5 new including referral-backed where ready

knowledge: Which P5 questions did you miss?
practical: Phase 5 gate pass criteria all met

tasks.text: Paper-to-Prod README: problem → architecture diagram → loop explained → tools/MCP → eval results (task success, citation validity, judge agreement, cost/run) → red-team summary → limitations. Deploy behind a spend cap + auth.
Second-pass DSA: 3 cold re-solves (mixed).
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “Paper-to-Prod README: problem → architecture diagram → loop explained → tools/MCP → eval r” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
5-minute demo video: question → live trajectory → verifier drops a claim → approval gate → brief delivered → eval dashboard → CI gate. Tag v1.0.
DSA gate attempt 1: 5 unseen mediums, ≤35 min each, narrating (2.5–3 h split across today/tomorrow). Log 4/5 or not, and gaps.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
10-min recall: explain yesterday’s “5-minute demo video: question → live trajectory → verifier drops a claim → approval gate →” aloud without notes; write one gap you found.
DSA gate attempt 1 (part 2) + debrief: pattern named within 3 minutes? complexity stated? communication?
Rapid recall: agent patterns, reliability math, LangGraph concepts, MCP security, eval methodology, serving internals — 30 questions aloud.

Take the Phase 5 gate (Assessments → P5): knowledge, coding (two-agent system from raw calls; LangGraph HITL; scorer), practical, explanation (framework defense; risk enumeration; enterprise RAG whiteboard). Record.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Permutations (Medium) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.

Applications sprint: Google (referral via Quiet Network if rapport exists — the ask is now specific and easy), direct applications tailored to JD keywords, 5 adjacent companies; update tracker; log what failed on any rejection so far.
Pramp mock coding interview (weekly). Debrief.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Subsets II (Medium) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.
Application pipeline (20 min): check saved searches, apply to 1–2 fitting roles within 48 h of posting, update tracker (status · next action · what failed).
Passed → tick m-agents; phase review. Failed → “fail → revisit” items before W44. If the DSA gate failed: set W44–W47 DSA slot to 90 min with 3 timed sets/week.
LinkedIn build-note: Paper-to-Prod is live — with eval numbers.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Combination Sum II (Medium) — no notes, ≤35 min each, narrate, state complexity; log time vs first pass.

Weekly revision — Shipping discipline: README → architecture → eval → limitations, Demo video, DSA gate, Phase 5 assessment: rewrite the key ideas from memory (no notes), then compare with your notes and fix the gaps. Reimplement two things from this week without looking.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Word Search (Medium, B75) · Palindrome Partitioning (Medium) — ≤35 min each, narrate, log time.
Weekly review: answer this week’s knowledge questions aloud, run the practical checks, then write the three notes (struggled / learned / improve) in Weekly Plan → Review. Update the tracking sheet.

JS/MERN spaced recall (Cycle 3 · interview mode) · Prototypes, classes, inheritance: Interview mode: explain how `class` desugars, then implement a tiny EventEmitter class with on/off/once/emit cold. Log misses in mistakes.md; if you fail the check, redo the matching module in Side Tracks → 🟨 JavaScript & MERN Refresher.
Plan next week: read W44’s objective and Day 1; move any unfinished 🔴 task into next week’s Day 1; confirm calendar blocks. Then rest — consistency beats intensity.
